title: Linux System Administrator
description: Master enterprise Linux operating systems, user management, file systems, systemd, process scheduling, shell automation, and security hardening.

goal.objective: Administer, automate, and harden Linux enterprise servers that form the foundational backbone of modern global computing.

learn.summary: Master Linux kernel architecture, the boot sequence, systemd service units, LVM disk storage, package managers, network troubleshooting, and shell scripting.
key_competencies: Linux Kernel, Boot Process & Systemd Management

capstone_projects.title: Automated Hardened Server Fleet Provisioning with Ansible & OpenSCAP
capstone_projects.description: Construct an automated infrastructure provisioning pipeline applying CIS Level 2 hardening benchmarks, auditd kernel logging, and automated compliance reporting.

capstone_projects.title: High-Availability Load Balancing & Failover Cluster with Keepalived & HAProxy
capstone_projects.description: Deploy a redundant dual-node load balancer cluster utilizing VRRP virtual IP failover, active health checking, zero-downtime reconfiguration, and SSL offloading.

interview_focus: Linux Boot Process (BIOS/UEFI -> GRUB -> Kernel -> Init / Systemd Targets)
Process Management & Signals (fork, exec, signals SIGTERM vs SIGKILL, Zombie vs Orphan Processes)
File System Architecture (Inodes, Superblocks, Hard Links vs Soft Links, VFS Layer)
Troubleshooting Server Performance (top, vmstat, iostat, sar, strace, lsof, netstat/ss)
Linux Networking Stack (iptables / nftables, routing tables, TCP socket states & tuning)

tree.name: Linux Fundamentals
tree.description: Master Linux operating system fundamentals: Kernel architecture, shell environments, file system hierarchies, user privileges, and package managers.

children.name: Command Line Interface Essentials
children.description: Master Bash command line essentials: Navigation, pipes, standard streams (stdin, stdout, stderr), redirection, text processing with grep, awk, sed, cut, and sort.

children.name: Filesystem Hierarchy, Permissions & Attributes
children.description: Navigate the Linux Filesystem Hierarchy Standard (FHS): Dissecting `/etc`, `/var`, `/usr`, `/proc`, `/sys`; managing POSIX permissions (`chmod`, `chown`), umask, and SUID/SGID/Sticky bits.

resources.title: How to Use the ip Command in Linux: A Beginner’s Guide (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: User, Group, and Sudo Management
children.description: Administer users and groups: Managing `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow`, `/etc/group`; configuring fine-grained sudoer privileges via `/etc/sudoers` with `visudo`.

resources.title: Systemd and Service Management (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: Software Package Management
children.description: Manage software packages across distributions: Debian/Ubuntu (APT, dpkg), RHEL/CentOS/Rocky (DNF, RPM), repository configuration, package pinning, and verifying GPG signatures.

children.name: Process Management and Job Control
children.description: Manage system processes: Process lifecycles, PID namespaces, signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL, SIGHUP), process monitoring with `ps`, `top`, `htop`, background jobs (`&`, `bg`, `fg`), and `nice`/`renice`.

children.name: Boot Process and System Initialization
children.description: Master Linux boot sequence: BIOS/UEFI firmware, GRUB2 bootloader, initramfs/initrd, kernel initialization, systemd targets, and analyzing boot times with `systemd-analyze`.

resources.title: How to Use the ip Command in Linux: A Beginner’s Guide (Learn Linux TV)

tree.name: Core System Services and Networking
tree.description: Configure essential Linux network services, remote SSH access, host-level firewalls, and scheduled cron automations.

resources.title: Red Hat Enterprise Linux Documentation - Networking Guide
Systemd and Service Management (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: Systemd Service Management
children.description: Master systemd service administration: Writing custom `.service`, `.socket`, and `.timer` unit files; managing service states with `systemctl`; and configuring auto-restart policies.

children.name: System Logging and Journalctl
children.description: Inspect and manage system logs: Querying binary logs with `journalctl`, configuring rsyslog, log rotation policies via `/etc/logrotate.conf`, and centralizing log forwarding.

children.name: Network Configuration and Troubleshooting
children.description: Configure network interfaces: `iproute2` suite (`ip addr`, `ip route`, `ip link`), NetworkManager (`nmcli`), bonding/bridging, testing connectivity with `ping`, `traceroute`, `curl`, and `ss`.

resources.title: How to Use the ip Command in Linux: A Beginner’s Guide (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: SSH and Secure Remote Access
children.description: Harden SSH access: Ed25519 key-pair authentication, `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` hardening (disabling root login, changing ports), SSH certificates, SSH agent forwarding, and bastion jump hosts.

resources.title: Systemd and Service Management (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: Firewall Management and Network Filtering
children.description: Manage host firewalls: Configuring `iptables`, `nftables`, `ufw`, and `firewalld`; defining packet filtering rules, NAT port forwarding, and connection state inspection.

resources.title: How To Configure a Firewall with UFW on Ubuntu 20.04

children.name: Scheduled Tasks and Job Automation
children.description: Automate scheduled jobs: User and system crontabs (`crontab -e`), `/etc/cron.*` directories, syntax conventions, and modern systemd timers for calendar-based tasks.

children.name: DNS and DHCP Fundamentals
children.description: Configure local name resolution and dynamic addressing: `/etc/resolv.conf`, `/etc/hosts`, systemd-resolved, querying DNS records with `dig`/`nslookup`, and DHCP client operations.

resources.title: How to Use the ip Command in Linux: A Beginner’s Guide (Learn Linux TV)

tree.name: Storage and Disk Management
tree.description: Manage physical and logical storage: Partitioning, file systems, LVM volume expansion, RAID arrays, and disaster recovery backups.

resources.title: Systemd and Service Management (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: Disk Partitioning and Filesystems
children.description: Partition and format block devices: MBR vs GPT partitioning with `fdisk`, `gdisk`, and `parted`; creating filesystems (ext4, XFS, Btrfs) with `mkfs`; and persistent `/etc/fstab` mounting.

children.name: Logical Volume Management (LVM)
children.description: Master Logical Volume Management (LVM): Physical Volumes (PV), Volume Groups (VG), Logical Volumes (LV); online volume resizing, thin provisioning, and LVM snapshots.

children.name: Advanced Storage Solutions and Concepts
children.description: Configure enterprise storage: Software RAID with `mdadm`, Network File System (NFS) exports, iSCSI initiator/target configurations, and exploring ZFS storage pools.

resources.title: How to Use the ip Command in Linux: A Beginner’s Guide (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: Backup, Restore and Disaster Recovery Strategies
children.description: Implement backup and recovery strategies: Snapshot-based backups, incremental rsync over SSH, archiving with tar/gzip, and disk cloning with `dd`.

resources.title: Systemd and Service Management (Learn Linux TV)

tree.name: Linux System Security and Hardening
tree.description: Harden enterprise Linux servers: Mandatory Access Control (SELinux/AppArmor), system auditing, kernel parameter tuning, and CVE vulnerability patching.

children.name: OS Hardening Best Practices
children.description: Implement CIS Benchmark hardening: Disabling unused kernel modules, securing shared memory (`/dev/shm`), setting login banners, and configuring PAM modules (`/etc/pam.d/`).

children.name: Advanced Access Control and Authentication
children.description: Master Mandatory Access Control (MAC): SELinux contexts, types, booleans, audit logs (`audit2allow`), and AppArmor profile configuration and enforcement.

resources.title: How to Use the ip Command in Linux: A Beginner’s Guide (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: Encryption and Secrets Management
children.description: Encrypt storage and manage credentials: Full disk encryption with LUKS (`cryptsetup`), file-level encryption, GPG keyrings, and secure credentials management.

resources.title: Systemd and Service Management (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: System Auditing and Compliance
children.description: Audit system security: Linux Audit Framework (`auditd`), writing `audit.rules` to monitor file integrity and privileged command execution, and OpenSCAP compliance scanning.

children.name: Vulnerability Management and Patching
children.description: Manage CVE patching: Automated security updates with `unattended-upgrades` (Debian) or `dnf-automatic` (RHEL), kernel live patching, and vulnerability auditing.

tree.name: Automation and Configuration Management
tree.description: Automate system administration: Writing production Bash scripts, Python automation tools, and orchestrating server fleets with Ansible.

children.name: Advanced Bash Scripting
children.description: Write advanced Bash scripts: Error handling (`set -euo pipefail`), command-line argument parsing with `getopts`, functions, trap signal handling, and regex pattern matching.

resources.title: Systemd and Service Management (Learn Linux TV)

children.name: Python Scripting for System Administration
children.description: Automate administration with Python: Interacting with system calls via `subprocess` and `os`, parsing JSON/YAML configs, and using Paramiko for automated SSH tasks.

children.name: Ansible Fundamentals
children.description: Manage configuration with Ansible: Writing declarative YAML playbooks, inventory management, core modules (`apt`, `yum`, `service`, `copy`, `template`), and idempotency.

children.name: Advanced Ansible: Roles, Vault, Galaxy, & Tower
children.description: Scale Ansible deployments: Authoring reusable Ansible Roles, encrypting secrets with Ansible Vault, Ansible Galaxy community collections, and AWX / Ansible Automation Platform.

children.description: Perform high-efficiency log analysis: Centralized log aggregation with Vector / Fluent Bit, querying logs in real time, and parsing log formats with custom regex.
